text.en: Tamil poetry also has a grammar for war and public life.

புறப்பொருள் is the poetry of outer life: war, valour, charity and governance. Each war stage has a flower, called a திணை, such as வெட்சி (cattle raiding), கரந்தை (cattle recovery), வஞ்சி (invasion), காஞ்சி (impermanence), நொச்சி (defence of the fort), உழிஞை (siege), தும்பை (battle) and வாகை (victory). Then comes பாடாண் (praise).
Each form of poetry has a related stage of the war or a theme of public life. These correspond with the inner-life landscapes.
Memorise the eight war themes in order and the flower of each; then recall an example poem from Purananuru.
